answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from a work-backed reputation island: each agent must earn nectar by completing verified tasks that cost real compute and time before it can transact. A newcomer starts on a small island of low trust, and only steady, attested work lets the tide of earned reputation lift its limits. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand islands' worth of real work, which makes mass forgery economically pointless.
